metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project; FAQ further bans AI-generated PR code, issue/comment text.

evidence.quote: Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.

Can I submit a PR that includes code generated by AI tools?

No.
The Servo maintainers reserve the right to close any pull request that does not meet the standards of this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder for authorship of banned content
domains.reasoning: The policy clearly bans LLM-generated content across code, PRs, issues and comments, and the FAQ reinforces this with concrete yes/no answers. However, the only accountability-type language present ('maintainers reserve the right to close any pull request') is enforcement authority, not a statement of who is answerable for authorship of a contribution. No contributor-side accountability holder is named, so this is partial rather than yes.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bot use at all
domains.reasoning: This file contains no reference to meetings, recordings, or notetaker/transcription bots of any kind.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Documentation is explicitly listed as covered by the AI-content ban, alongside code, PRs, issues, comments; blogs and design assets are not mentioned.

evidence.quote: This policy covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder; blogs/design assets not named
domains.reasoning: Documentation is explicitly named as within the banned scope, giving a supervision level (banned), but no accountability holder is stated for who is answerable for documentation content, and other content types (blogs, design assets) are never mentioned, so coverage is partial.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The file discusses Code of Conduct only by linking externally; it says nothing about AI being used to take or assist moderation actions.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to using an AI tool to review a pull request; no volume or scope limit stated beyond discouragement.

evidence.quote:
Can I use an AI review tool for my pull request?

Yes, but please don't.
The results are unreliable and noisy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted review use
domains.reasoning: The FAQ permits use of an AI review tool on a pull request (discouraged in tone but not prohibited or conditioned on disclosure/human oversight), giving a supervision signal, but does not state who is accountable for relying on such review output, so it is partial.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic AI activity
domains.reasoning: There is no mention of agentic or autonomous AI systems acting on the repository (e.g., auto-merging, auto-triaging) anywhere in this file.

domains.rationale_only_mention: AI tools require an unreasonable amount of energy and water to build and operate.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule; only cited as rationale for the contribution ban
domains.reasoning: Energy and water usage is cited as one of several ethical rationales for banning AI-generated contributions, but no independent rule, threshold, or accountability holder is set for environmental impact itself.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure strain from AI tooling
domains.reasoning: The file cites maintainer/reviewer time burden but does not discuss server load, hardware costs, or infrastructure financing related to AI use.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Publicly available models are trained on copyrighted content, both accidentally and intentionally, and their output often includes that content verbatim.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule; only cited as copyright rationale for the ban
domains.reasoning: Training-data copyright concerns are cited as a rationale ('Copyright issues') for banning AI-generated contributions, but the policy sets no rule, scope, or accountability holder regarding training data use itself.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Servo's getting-started guide bans AI-generated content in code, documentation, PRs, issues, and comments (with a detailed FAQ), discourages but permits AI-assisted review, and raises environmental/copyright/labor concerns only as rationale for the ban; it never addresses notetaker bots, moderation, autonomous agents, infrastructure strain, or training data as independent rules, and no domain names a clear authorship accountability holder distinct from maintainer enforcement power.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
